name: Reality Mechanics Diagram
tag: An interactive diagram that maps 14 centers of the body to 14 universal laws for study and reflection.

scenarios.title: Take a guided tour
scenarios.ask: Walk me through {centers} of the 14 centers, about {mins} each, in {view} view.
steps: Diagram
Highlighted {centers} center(s) on the body map and drew the line to each linked law.
Guide
Read a short description of each center and its law, in the app's own framework.
Reflection
Added one question per center to think about during the day.
Journal
Saved your notes so the next tour starts at center {=min(14, centers + 1)}.
followups: Is this an anatomy or medical chart?
No. It is a contemplative study model, not anatomy and not medical advice.
Can I see all 14 at once?
Yes. The full view shows all 14 centers and laws, and you can tap any pair to open it.

scenarios.title: Run a workshop
scenarios.ask: I'm teaching {people} people in a {length} session. Set up the diagram for the room.
steps: Presenter
Switched to presenter mode with large labels for a projector.
Planner
Fit {=min(14, floor(length / 10))} centers into the session at about 10 minutes each.
Groups
Split the room into {=ceil(people / 6)} groups, each with a center to discuss.
Handouts
Made {people} printable handouts with the diagram and reflection questions.
followups: Can participants follow on their phones?
Yes. They scan a code and see the diagram move as you present.
Can I add my own notes?
Yes. Presenter notes stay on your screen and do not show on the projector.

scenarios.title: Start a daily practice
scenarios.ask: Give me a {days}-day practice, {mins} a day, cycling through the 14 centers.
steps: Planner
Cycled the 14 centers across {days} days, so each comes up about {=round(days / 14, 1)} times.
Reminders
Set a daily reminder with the day's center and law.
Reflection
Wrote one prompt for each day.
Tracker
Tracks streaks and shows which centers you return to most.
followups: What if I miss a day?
The plan picks up where you left off. Your streak resets, but your notes stay.
No. The practice is for reflection and study, not medical advice.
